questions.question: What does SWOT stand for? Explain the difference between internal and external factors.
questions.expected_answer: Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats. Internal factors (strengths, weaknesses) are inside the business and can be controlled or changed. External factors (opportunities, threats) are in the environment outside the business and cannot be controlled, only responded to.

questions.question: Complete a SWOT analysis for a juice stall at a school sports day with one point in each box.
questions.expected_answer: Example: S: team has a blender and a good recipe; low-cost fruit from a family farm. W: no experience; limited cold storage. O: hot sports day, many thirsty spectators; no other juice stall. T: competitor selling cold cooldrinks; fruit prices rise; event cancelled for rain. (Accept reasonable answers with correct categories.)

questions.question: Explain how a business should use a SWOT analysis after completing it, with one example.
questions.expected_answer: Turn it into actions: use strengths to take opportunities, fix or reduce weaknesses, prepare for threats. E.g. weakness 'only one pot' → borrow a second pot; threat 'rain' → arrange indoor space and a backup product.
